text:
Ajay: Quick heads-up — ran the Q4 capacity forecast this morning, and the burst policy is the main driver of cost variance. We should tighten guardrails before the holiday spike.
Maria: Can you share the headline numbers?
Ajay: Short version: steady-state demand ~1200 GPU-hours/day. Holiday multiplier ~1.6 -> peak ~1920 GPU-hours/day. Current burst allowance (up to 40%) pushes us past prepaid commitments and spikes spend. Recommend conservative burst caps: business-hours 8% (soft), off-hours 15% (soft), plus region sticky reserve.
Li: How did you get steady-state -> peak? quick math pls.
Ajay: Used production telemetry: avg_tokens_per_min * avg_session_minutes * concurrent_sessions, converted to tokens_per_gpu_hour (observed ~1.2B tokens/GPU-hour for LlamaX-13B quantized). Quick calc: 
```
steady_gpu_hours = (avg_tokens_per_min * avg_minutes * active_sessions * 60) / tokens_per_gpu_hour
```
(This is in the notebook I pushed to infra/forecasts).
Carla: Lowering burst that much will affect tail latency for sudden multi-tenant surges. Any mitigation? :thinking:  
Ajay: Agreed. Mitigations: keep a sticky reserve of 100 GPUs in us-west for low-latency traffic, enable soft-queueing (TTL 60s) with backpressure to clients, and set autoscaler cooldown to 120s to avoid oscillation. Also implement regional spillover: if queue_len > 200, route excess to us-east.
deploy-bot: [deploy] autoscaler-config v2 promoted to staging by Ajay at 2025-11-15T08:05:12Z
Maria: Paste the proposed autoscaler snippet so SRE + Platform can review.
Ajay: Snippet: 
```
{"burst_cap_pct":8, "off_hours_burst_pct":15, "min_warm_gpus":100, "cooldown_seconds":120, "queue_ttl_seconds":60, "spill_threshold":200}
```
Li: Where do we put per-region overrides? We need tighter caps in APAC because capacity is scarcer.
Ajay: Routing policy supports per-region overrides in /etc/redwood/autoscaler/overrides.yaml. Example line I plan to add for apac: 
```
apac: { burst_cap_pct: 5, min_warm_gpus: 20 }
```
Carla: For the canary: we should run in us-west-2 pool only, monitor `burst_util_pct`, `p99_latency`, `eviction_rate`. Alert if evictions > 0.5% or p99 > 1.2x baseline. I'll own the rollout.
Ajay: Canary plan: apply to canary pool at 09:00 UTC tomorrow, 30m watch window, then step to other hosted pools if clean. Command I'll run: 
```
kubectl apply -f autoscaler-v2.json && kubectl rollout status deploy/autoscaler --watch
```
Maria: Cost impact estimate? Finance needs numbers before we commit.
Ajay: Rough monthly savings ~ $45k (from reducing average burst usage). There's also reduced variability which helps with committed capacity planning. I pushed the forecast table to infra/forecasts/q4-burst-analysis.csv.
Li: Any perf diff expected vs current (latency/cold starts)?
Ajay: Expect slight increase in cold-start tail for large model invocations during extreme spikes if reserve exhausted. But with sticky reserve + soft queue we should keep SLA. We'll also pre-warm top-10 pinned models during predicted peak windows.
ops-bot: Reminder: scheduled maintenance window 2025-11-15T09:00Z - 2025-11-15T09:30Z (capacity-plan team).
Carla: ack :thumbsup: I'll add dashboard panels and the alert rules. Also pinging capacity-planning to freeze hardware purchases Nov 14-18 so we don't overprovision for the brief spike.
Maria: Please add a metric for `burst_util_pct` to the global perf dashboard and a heatmap for regional queue lengths.
Li: One more thing — can we make the burst cap adaptive to roll-forward quickly if external partner traffic (predictable high-volume) is flagged? Maybe a temporary override API that requires two approvers.
Ajay: Good idea. I'll add an `override_window` flag and an approver workflow: `POST /v1/autoscaler/override?expires=60m` requires 2 approvers. No unilateral bypass.
Carla: After canary, if stable, we'll propagate to dedicated pools on Nov 20. I'll run a small cost-sim with dedicated pricing to confirm savings.
Maria: noted, leaving a finance ticket for the $45k delta.
Ajay: TL;DR: apply conservative burst caps, keep sticky reserve, soft-queue and regional spillover, canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC in us-west-2, monitors + alerts ready.
Carla: On it. Will post results in this thread.
Maria: thanks everyone.
